findings.title: Specific client deny permissions are bypassed when a broad VIEW permission exists
findings.body: canView(ClientModel) first calls no-arg canView(), which returns true whenever the caller has a VIEW permission on the all-clients resource. That short-circuits the method before hasPermission(client, VIEW), which is the only path that evaluates the client-specific resource. As a result, a negative VIEW permission on an individual client is ignored for any admin who also has all-clients VIEW; the admin can still view the denied client. This differs from the intended FGAP behavior exercised by the user-resource tests, where a specific resource overrides the all-resource. The no-arg canView()/all-clients shortcut should not be used here (or must only short-circuit on legacy admin roles), and a test should cover all-clients VIEW plus a client-specific negative VIEW.

findings.title: Client role mapping checks no longer honor MANAGE_CLIENTS
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles return only hasPermission(client, scope). They do not delegate to the V1 implementation or otherwise check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), unlike the other overrides in this class. With V2 enabled, an administrator who only has the standard manage-clients role can no longer add client roles, add composites, or map client-scope roles; those endpoints will reject the request. The new tests grant explicit MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE permissions, so they do not catch this regression. At minimum these methods need the MANAGE_CLIENTS check (and should consider a MANAGE grant if MANAGE is meant to be inclusive).

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Clients scopes/resources
findings.body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin permissions client. Adding the CLIENTS resource type to SCHEMA only affects realms initialized after this change. After upgrading a realm that already has the admin-permissions client, the Clients scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite, etc.) and the 'Clients' all-resource do not exist. Creating Clients permissions then fails scope validation, and client permission evaluation can fall through to a missing all-clients resource. The existing admin permissions client must be reconciled/updated to add missing scopes and type resources, or a migration is required.

findings.title: Null all-clients resource is dereferenced during client permission checks
findings.body: When no specific client resource exists, hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) obtains the Clients all-resource and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking resource for null. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource cannot be found (for example a realm initialized before the Clients resource type was added, or a partially initialized admin permissions client). The authorization check then throws NPE/500 instead of denying. The no-arg hasPermission(String) already handles a missing resource; this method should do the same before calling findByResource.

findings.title: Client resources are not resolved to client IDs for permission representations
findings.body: getResourceName only handles the USERS resource type. Client-specific resources are stored under the internal client UUID, so for CLIENTS the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), producing a UUID/null instead of the clientId, and the all-clients resource is not displayed as 'All clients'. This makes permission/resource REST output for the new Clients resource type unreadable or inconsistent with the Users implementation. Add a CLIENTS branch analogous to USERS, including the all-clients case.

findings.title: Client removal handling is skipped for V2 and still throws when both features are enabled
findings.body: The listener body is now guarded only by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1). When only V2 is enabled, deleting a client no longer triggers any cleanup for V2 client-specific resources/permissions, so those can remain as orphans. When both V1 and V2 are enabled, management(...) returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client deletion can fail. Handle the V2 case explicitly (cleanup or no-op) instead of relying only on the V1 feature flag.

findings.title: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope is not exercised
findings.body: The PR adds MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE to the Clients scopes and implements canMapClientScopeRoles, but the new test only grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE and never tests mapping roles to a client scope. A regression in the new client-scope role authorization path would not be detected. Add a test that grants MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE and exercises the corresponding client-scope role operation.
